In the sentence “The fact that he had lied upset everyone,” the clause “that he had lied” is a:
questions.why: The clause explains the noun 'fact' and acts as a noun in apposition. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “to carry coals to Newcastle”:
questions.why: Newcastle was a coal-producing town, so supplying coal there is pointless. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Change into a complex sentence: “Work hard, or you will fail.”
opts: If you do not work hard, you will fail.
Unless you do not work hard, you will fail.
If you work hard, you will fail.
Unless you work hard, you will not fail.
questions.why: 'Or' (otherwise) becomes 'if ... not'; 'unless' already carries negation. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: “She would have recovered sooner had she ____ the prescribed diet.”
questions.why: 'Had she + past participle' is the inverted third conditional. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: “It is essential that he ____ present at the meeting.”
questions.why: After 'it is essential that', the subjunctive (bare infinitive) is used. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: She said, “I used to play tennis.”
opts: She said that she had used to play tennis.
She said that she used to play tennis.
She said that she has used to play tennis.
She said that she would used to play tennis.
questions.why: 'Used to' does not backshift. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: In the sentence “Hard as he tried, he could not lift the stone,” the clause “Hard as he tried” is a:
questions.why: 'Hard as he tried' means 'though he tried hard': concession. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “pragmatic”:
questions.why: 'Pragmatic' means dealing with things realistically; 'idealistic' is the opposite. GPSC-style practice item.
